name: RimeholtYardangField
intent: A wind-carved yardang field of only one to three enormous near-black granite fins, each a high blunt prow falling down a long low tail, every crest carrying one bright unbroken line of packed snow and streaming long bright spindrift in one direction, with a wind-cut arch on the highest crest and the road weaving between their tails.
variation: layout: spine (one great fin) / pair (two fins flanking the road) / echelon (three staggered fins down one flank) / slalom (two fins with heads at opposite ends of the field)
fin size: 1-3 fins, each 14-28 cells long and 3.4-7.2 cells half-breadth, crests 18-42 studs high, a high blunt prow falling to a long low tail
road: 1-3 S-bends swinging 4-8 cells, entering and leaving anywhere on the south and north borders, a 6-cell-wide lane kept open through every fin
wind shear: every crest line leans 2.2-4 cells the same way, east or west, with a wandering crest and a wind gap cut across some fins
surface and crests: pale drift snow with 2-4 long wind streaks and one lee ice patch, sparse fell grass, and every fin carrying one unbroken bright snow line along its crest
requests: A yaw or route on effects, so every crest plume streams along the field's one wind; a worm's direction is seeded and can differ from crest to crest.
A sculpt kind with a smooth streamlined fin profile; per-cell lifts step the fins' flanks at cell resolution.

critic_pass1.best_shot: shots seed 2, the arch on the crest
critic_pass1.why: Good seed variety, but fins read as bleachers, grey on grey, and the spindrift is muddy.

critic_pass2.best_shot: shots seed 1, the arch on the crest
critic_pass2.why: Layouts differ, but the fins still read as stepped bleachers grey on grey and the spindrift is nearly invisible.

critic_pass3.best_shot: feature-shots seed 3, the field from the south-east
critic_pass3.why: Fins are now near-black prows with tails and an arch, and the seeds vary most in count and threading; flanks still read as stacked cubes and the game camera sees a black wall.

final_notes:
# D: wind-carved yardang field

Keep: the fins are now near-black, fewer and shaped (seed 3 "the field from the south-east" is a single prow falling to a long tail with the arch on its crest), and the crest-wind set piece streams in one direction.

1. The flanks are still a staircase of identical cubes; from "the arch on the crest" they read as stacked crates. Larger steps (fewer, taller) on the prow and a smooth taper to the tail would read as wind-cut rock.
2. The bright snow line is broken into separate pale squares on most crests; make it one unbroken pale ridge so the fin has a lit edge from the game camera.
3. From the game camera (seeds 1 and 3) a black wall fills half the frame with nothing on it; frame the camera on the tail and the road, with the prow behind, or lower the fins nearest the south edge.

Last round: answered the grey-on-grey (granite now near-black) and fewer fins with prow and tail; partly answered the spindrift (a long streaming streak in the set piece); not answered the bleacher rhythm of the flanks.
